content:
Hello,

The automated Palomar review of my stalex444/pdt-hodge-lie-generationrepo dated 2026-09-13T22:44:08Z, states:

Mechanical verification succeeded, and the mathematical account passed the substantive editorial checks, but the egregiously off-topic MSC2020 classification must be corrected.

Its only requested change is removal of MSC2020 code 68V20. The page explicitly
instructs me to update the repository and submit the corrected commit as a new
submission. I have a screenshot documenting the review and that instruction.

That exact one-line correction is now published here:
https://github.com/stalex444/pdt-hodge-lie-generation/commit/63b357f6b4adf85c888036e148bd8f8f645cb1b4

The Lean proofs and statements are unchanged and I made the single code change requested. However, I am now rate-limited from submitting the same submission with the single change for 3 days.

Could an operator reset the submission waiting interval for my GitHub account,
stalex444, so I can submit the requested single correction? I am following the
review's dictates and would appreciate help completing that process without having to wait another 3 days.

Thank you :)

Hi @Stephanie Alexander, first, please please remember not to use an LLM to generate text that you are posting as yourself here on Zulip. This is contrary to the community expectations here, and will result in messages being junked, and accounts suspended.

But second, the rate limits are intentionally automatic and quite generous: in order to have hit a 3 day rate limiter, it means you've already been hitting our backend pretty hard. So, to be honest, I would prefer to leave it in place. If there's some actual need for urgency, I'll listen, but otherwise, please avoid whatever it was that you did in the first place to reach that rate limit, and be patient. :-)

Thank you for the response, @Kim Morrison. I am set to leave town shortly and just wanted to finish the submission before I lost access to my main computer for awhile. I will note that I had an issue with a previous Palomar submission at the Challenge rendering stage (which Palomar acknowledged was a problem on its end). I tried to work around this Palomar hiccup by just revising/resubmitting but ultimately gave up, and I believe that contributed to the rate limit issue here.

As an aside, I just posted about Palomar in response to an X thread by the arXiv editor-in-chief regarding the rise of unverified math on arXiv. He was suggesting the need for something like Palomar. Here is a link to that post in case someone from Palomar wants to contribute more to that conversation. https://x.com/3DAnomaly/status/2099256466112659482?s=20

Thank you again :)

Looking at the issue, it was a nit. Metadata had (apparently) wrong category 68V20 = "Formalization of mathematics in connection with theorem provers", an understandable mistake for a lean proof.

please avoid whatever it was that you did in the first place to reach that rate limit

This isn't a very inviting response for future contributors. As far as I can tell, the people in this channel hitting multi-day delays are from good faith submissions that verified locally.
